stories.headline: Stocks extend sell-off as Anthropic IPO fails to calm AI worries
stories.summary: US stock futures fell sharply Friday, with the S&P 500 on pace for a sixth straight day of losses and the Dow dipping below 50,000, approaching correction territory. S&P 500 futures were down about 0.8% and Nasdaq-100 futures down roughly 1.7%, as broad anxiety over AI spending, financing, and safety persisted despite Anthropic's blockbuster IPO. Asian semiconductor stocks also fell, extending the global tech selloff.

stories.headline: AMD shares slide 7.7% after Hunterbrook short-seller report ties firmware to blacklisted Chinese firm
stories.summary: AMD stock fell as much as 11.2% intraday and closed down 7.7% at $489.19 Thursday after short seller Hunterbrook Media reported that newer AMD firmware kept showing up at IEIT Systems, a Chinese server maker blacklisted by the US in 2025; Hunterbrook's affiliated fund is short the stock. AMD said the claims misrepresent its business practices and relationships, and shares fell a further 6% in Friday premarket trading. The drop follows a nearly 45% rally over the prior five sessions, from $404.40 on November 5 to $585.30 on November 12.

stories.headline: Anthropic shares retreat after record $81.3 billion IPO, but hold above offer price
stories.summary: Anthropic (ANT) priced its IPO at $83 per share on November 18, the largest offering on record at $81.3 billion raised, and opened at $111.50 on its Nasdaq debut November 19 before closing its first day at $97.17. Shares fell further Friday amid the broader AI-driven market selloff, though they remain above the IPO price; analysts including Melius ($155 target) and Needham ($150 target) initiated coverage with bullish price targets. Yahoo Finance cautioned investors to stay focused on fundamentals rather than first-day pop hype.

stories.headline: Nvidia's post-earnings slide deepens into sixth straight day
stories.summary: Nvidia shares fell another 3.2-3.4% Friday to around $141, extending a six-session decline since last week's earnings beat as broader AI-sector weakness and risk-off sentiment overshadow the results. The continued slide in the AI bellwether is weighing heavily on major indices given Nvidia's large index weighting.

stories.headline: South Korea and Japan stock markets sink more than 4% amid global tech rout
stories.summary: South Korea's Kospi and Japan's Nikkei 225 both dropped more than 4% as the AI-driven selloff in US tech stocks spread to Asian markets, hitting semiconductor and AI-linked names particularly hard. The sharp overnight declines set a weak tone for US futures heading into Friday's session.

stories.headline: Bitcoin hits near five-month low below $62,000 as AI rout batters risk appetite
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell as much as 3.8% to below $62,000, its lowest level since roughly July, as the broader selloff in AI and risk assets spread into crypto markets. Gold futures also fell about 3%, a sign that the recent market stress is driving broad de-risking rather than a flight to traditional safe havens.

stories.headline: AMD, Broadcom and CoreWeave stocks mixed as Nvidia tops Q3 earnings estimates
stories.summary: Nvidia's better-than-expected fiscal third-quarter results sparked a mixed reaction across AI chip and infrastructure names, with shares of AMD, Broadcom, and TSMC rising while CoreWeave and Nebius also rallied in sympathy. The divergent moves reflect lingering investor uncertainty about the durability of AI capital spending even after a strong earnings beat.

stories.headline: Gas prices drop below $4 per gallon as consumer sentiment data looms
stories.summary: National average gasoline prices fell below the $4 per gallon threshold ahead of Friday's final University of Michigan consumer sentiment reading, offering a modest offset to households amid the broader market turbulence. The sentiment report is a closely watched gauge of consumer mood heading into the holiday shopping season.
